stem:
A student investigates the collision of two gliders A and B on a linear air-track, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The light gate is connected to a timer. A card of length *L* is attached to glider B. The mass of glider B and the card is *m*. Glider B is initially at rest.

The student releases glider A so that it travels at a constant velocity *u* towards the stationary glider B. The gliders collide and then separate.

The card on glider B passes through the light gate. The student records the time *t* for the card to pass through the light gate from the timer.

The student changes the mass of glider B and repeats the experiment.

It is suggested that the velocity *v* of glider B as it passes through the light gate and *m* are related by the equation

$v = \frac{2uA}{m + A}$

where *A* is the mass of glider A.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of $\frac{1}{v}$ on the *y*-axis against *m* on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *m* and *t* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of $\frac{1}{v}$ / s cm⁻¹ in Table 2.1 where $\frac{1}{v} = \frac{t}{L}$

and *L* = 5.0 ± 0.1 cm.

Include the absolute uncertainties in $\frac{1}{v}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of $\frac{1}{v}$ / s cm⁻¹ against *m* / g.

Include error bars for $\frac{1}{v}$.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Both lines should be clearly labelled.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine values of *u* and *A*. Include appropriate units.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The experiment is repeated. Determine the mass *m* of glider B and the card when *t* has a value of 0.50 s.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A card attached to glider B passes through a light gate on an air-track as gliders A and B approach each other.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for m in grams, t in seconds, and 1/v in s cm⁻¹; the first two columns contain six sets of values and the last column is blank.
A blank graph grid with 1/v in s cm⁻¹ on the vertical axis and m in grams on the horizontal axis.
